papers.title: Attention-Guided Transformer Network for Polyp Segmentation in Colonoscopy Images
papers.abstract: Polyp segmentation is crucial for early colorectal cancer diagnosis. We propose a transformer-based network with a multi-scale attention decoder that captures both local and global contextual information. Experiments on three public datasets demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance with a Dice score of 0.923 on Kvasir-SEG and 0.891 on CVC-ClinicDB. Our approach shows particular strength in segmenting polyps with unclear boundaries.

papers.title: Efficient U-Net with Depthwise Separable Convolutions for Real-Time Polyp Segmentation
papers.abstract: Real-time polyp segmentation remains challenging for deployment in clinical settings. We propose EfficientU-Net, a lightweight CNN architecture using depthwise separable convolutions that achieves competitive accuracy with significantly fewer parameters. Our model achieves 0.891 Dice on Kvasir-SEG while running at 120 FPS on a standard GPU. The model has only 2.1M parameters compared to 31M for standard U-Net, making it suitable for edge deployment.

papers.title: Cross-Domain Polyp Segmentation via Style Transfer and Domain Adaptation
papers.abstract: Polyp segmentation models trained on one colonoscopy dataset often fail on images from different centers due to domain shift. We propose a domain adaptation framework that uses style transfer to harmonize image appearances across domains. Our method incorporates a domain discriminator and style-matching loss. Experiments show a 12% improvement in Dice when transferring from Kvasir-SEG to ETIS-Larib without target domain labels. The approach reduces the need for per-center annotation.
